from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Plane-Cone Intersection", [
            "A double-napped cone meets a flat plane.",
            "Tilting the plane creates different conic shapes.",
            "Circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas emerge."
        ])
        
        # Cone: Two cones apex-to-apex
        # Note: Cone in Manim is not a standard mobject; using Surface or similar logic if needed,
        # but fixing the TypeError by correcting the argument names if they were mislabeled.
        # Manim's Cone is defined as Cone(base_radius=..., height=...)
        cone = VGroup(
            Cone(base_radius=1, height=1.5, direction=DOWN),
            Cone(base_radius=1, height=1.5, direction=UP)
        ).set_color(WHITE)
        
        plane = Polygon(
            [-1.5, -0.5, 0], [1.5, -0.5, 0], [1.5, 0.5, 0], [-1.5, 0.5, 0],
            color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.4
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_in_area(cone, "B2", "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(cone))
        self.play(FadeIn(plane.rotate(PI/6)))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        
        # Highlight intersection (ellipse)
        intersection = Circle(radius=0.7, color="#FF00FF").rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(intersection, "C3")
        self.play(Create(intersection))
        
        # Tilt animation
        self.play(Rotate(plane, angle=PI/8, about_point=self.grid["C3"]))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(cone), FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(intersection))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Two spheres define the ellipse's foci.",
            "Points of tangency mark the focal spots.",
            "Distance sums stay constant for any point.",
            "This defines the elegant ellipse structure.",
            "Geometry connects points to simple curves."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of the Ellipse", lecture_lines)
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0)
        
        # Setup objects
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=4, height=2.5, color="#FF4500")
        foci = VGroup(Dot(color=YELLOW), Dot(color=YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        foci[0].move_to(ellipse.get_center() + LEFT * 1.2)
        foci[1].move_to(ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT * 1.2)
        
        p = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def get_ellipse_point():
            return ellipse.point_from_proportion(p.get_value())
            
        point_on_ellipse = Dot(color=WHITE)
        point_on_ellipse.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_ellipse_point()))
        
        line1 = Line(foci[0].get_center(), point_on_ellipse.get_center(), color=BLUE)
        line2 = Line(foci[1].get_center(), point_on_ellipse.get_center(), color=BLUE)
        
        line1.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(foci[0].get_center(), point_on_ellipse.get_center()))
        line2.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(foci[1].get_center(), point_on_ellipse.get_center()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(foci))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        self.add(point_on_ellipse, line1, line2)
        self.play(p.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(Indicate(ellipse))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_opacity(1)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Plane angles dictate sphere behavior.",
            "Parabolas need only one tangent sphere.",
            "Hyperbolas place spheres in different nappes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Generalizing to Parabola and Hyperbola", lecture_lines)
        
        # Representations
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2, direction=DOWN).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        cone.set_fill(opacity=0.3).set_stroke(WHITE, width=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(cone, "A2", "D5")
        self.add(cone)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")
        parabola_path = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5 * t**2 - 0.5, 0]), t_range=[-1, 1]
        ).set_color("#32CD32")
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_path, "E3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(parabola_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#1E90FF")
        hyperbola_path = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5 * t**2 + 0.5, 0]), t_range=[-1, 1]
        ).set_color("#1E90FF")
        hyperbola_path_2 = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, -(0.5 * t**2 + 0.5), 0]), t_range=[-1, 1]
        ).set_color("#1E90FF")
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_path, "E3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_path_2, "F3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Transform(parabola_path, hyperbola_path))
        self.play(Create(hyperbola_path_2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Real-World Application", [
            "Dandelin spheres bridge 3D and 2D.",
            "Satellite dishes utilize these precise properties.",
            "Planetary orbits follow these geometric laws."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a summary of conic sections
        summary = VGroup(
            Text("3D Spatial Geometry", font_size=24, color=BLUE),
            Text("↓ Bridge ↓", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
            Text("2D Conic Equations", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(summary, "B2", "D5")
        self.play(Write(summary))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition to satellite dish visual
        dish = Parabolas = VGroup(
            Arc(radius=2, start_angle=PI/2, angle=PI, color=RED),
            Dot(point=[0, 0, 0], color=YELLOW) # Focal point
        )
        self.place_at_grid(dish, "C3", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        label = Text("Application: Satellite Dish", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "E3")
        
        self.play(FadeOut(summary), FadeIn(dish), Write(label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Indicate(dish[1])) # Highlight focal point
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Planetary orbits
        orbit = Ellipse(width=3, height=2, color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(orbit, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Transform(dish, orbit), label.animate.set_text("Application: Planetary Orbits"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(3)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(dish), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title))

outline.topic: Unlocking Conic Sections: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres
outline.target_audience: High school geometry or early undergraduate students

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Plane-Cone Intersection
sections.content: Briefly define a double-napped cone and a cutting plane. Introduce the intuitive idea that changing the angle of the plane relative to the cone's axis generates different shapes: circle, ellipse, parabola, and hyperbola.
sections.example: Visualizing a flashlight beam hitting a wall at different angles.

sections.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Dandelin Spheres'—spheres placed inside the cone that are tangent to both the cone and the cutting plane. Explain that the points of tangency are the keys to understanding conic properties.
sections.example: An animation of two glowing spheres inflating inside a glass cone until they touch a tilted transparent plane.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Ellipse
sections.content: Focus on the ellipse. Show that the two points where the two Dandelin spheres touch the plane are the 'foci' of the ellipse. Explain how the sum of distances from any point on the ellipse to these two spheres remains constant.
sections.example: A 'string-and-tacks' animation showing the sum of distances remaining constant as the perimeter point moves.

sections.title: Generalizing to Parabola and Hyperbola
sections.content: Explain how shifting the plane's angle changes the behavior of the spheres. For a parabola, the plane is parallel to the cone's slant, leaving only one sphere. For a hyperbola, the spheres are placed in different nappes of the cone.
sections.example: A transformation animation where a 'Robot Arm' tilts the cutting plane, watching the spheres grow or shift position to accommodate the new conic shape.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize that Dandelin spheres bridge 3D spatial geometry and 2D conic equations. Conclude with how these properties are used in satellite dish design and planetary orbit calculations.
sections.example: A satellite dish (hyperbolic/parabolic) focusing incoming radio waves from deep space into a single sensor point.
